newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 20.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The English cricket team credits its success in the first Test against Australia to a computer program called StatsMaster, developed by Melbourne company Prowess Systems. The program allows coaches like England's David Lloyd to turn TV footage of sporting events into an exhaustive database. Page 1.

The first Australian Stock Exchange survey in three years has revealed there has been a sharp lift in the number of Australian adults investing directly, up from 16 per cent to 20 per cent, and overall 34 per cent of the adult population own shares as indviduals or through funds. Page 1.

Federal Court Justice Donald Hill, who dissented from a majority judgement yesterday which ruled that if taxpayers are bankrupted by an Australian Taxation Office assessment then they no longer have a legal right to challenge the assessment, warned yesteray the decision could lead to an abuse of taxpayers'
rights. Page 3.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics' fourth edition of Australian Social Trends, released yesterday, showed jobs done for the home, such as personal service workers, along with dental nurses and tourist guides, are now among the fastest growing areas of emloyment in the domestic economy. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Senate superannuation committee is investigating reforms that will allow Federal politicians who are voted out after a short period to receive taxpayer-funded low-tax redundancy payouts. The system will give MPs, who receive no termination payments, nough funds to tide them over as they readjust to private life. Page 1.

The 1997 Australian Stock Exchange Shareholder Survey released yesterday shows the number of players in the sharemarket has almost doubled this decade, and there is a shift towards women and low income earners investing. The floating of
household names sch as Westpac, Qantas and the Commonwealth Bank has encouraged investment. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard came under attack yesterday for spending a day at the second cricket Test during his overseas trip, and was disappointed to learn from Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor that the ground at Lord's was the wettest he'd seen it Page 1.

Following three days of probing in Federal Parliament, Small Business Minister Geoff Prosser admitted he had called Coles Myer director and senior Liberal figure Nick Greiner for assistance for his brother Stephen and his private business interests. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Twenty five New South Wales Labor Party backbenchers vowed to cross the floor over the proposed A$22 billion sell off of the State's electricity industry unless the proposal had the support of the unions and party members. The move places the
proposal injeopardy and sees the members risking expulsion. Page 1.

The A$800 million proposal by David Brice and the East Asia Property Group to resolve the East Circular Quay controversy gained a boost yesterday when former New South Wales Premier Neville Wran joined a top-level team of corporate and financial advisers to assist Brice. Page 1.

As it was announced yesterday that the first show to be performed at the Lyric Theatre at Sydney's new casino will be Jerome Kern's Showboat, the casino's new name, Star City, came under question as being more crass than class. Page 1.

Clerk of the Senate Harry Evans yesterday advised the parliamentary committee evaluating the performance of the National Crime Authority that there was no legal impediment to material relating to the alleged A$66.5 million fraud case against former EldersIXL boss John Elliott. Page 1.
THE AGE

The disclosure by Labor Senator Stephen Conroy in Federal Parliament of controversial National Crime Authority material relating to businessman John Elliott may force the Federal Parliamentary inquiry into the National Crime Authority to be abandoned. Page 1.

Brett Leskie, the father of 14-month-old Jaidyn Leskie who was abducted on the weekend, has pleaded for the boy's safe return, believing the boy still to be alive. Police are no closer to closing the case after five days of searching and
interviewing thoe close to the boy. Page 1.

Melbourne has lost the Australian premiere of Garth Drabinsky's musical Showboat, which was due to open at the Regent Theatre in April, to Sydney Harbour Casino's new Lyric Theatre, but has picked up the opening season of Ragtime. The loss of Showboat coes amid fears that a "casino culture" is swamping Melbourne's art market. Page 1.

Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge has ruled out a national summit on drug abuse, despite concerns across Australia about the country's level of heroin abuse. However, Wooldridge will be pushing for increasing the campaign against drug use and wil urge the States to concentrate on a uniform approach to prevention and treatment. Page 3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
